subject: Edge NAT + control/data-plane concordance — design review
body:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge NAT + control/data-plane concordance — design review

Team —

I've attached the latest draft of the control-plane / data-plane interface (v2) and an egress/NAT sketch from the Packly trial site. We need a short readout and explicit callouts for:
- How the control-plane (CP) will call back to the management endpoints if the data-plane (DP) is behind a NAT
- Preferred connectivity pattern for heartbeat/tracing (persistent TLS tunnel vs periodic outbound calls)
- What we will require as proof-of-connectivity for cutover (ports, observability hooks)

Immediate asks:
1) Irene — can you review the CP callback options and flag anything that would break our KVCACHE regional routing?
2) Marissa — please confirm the ops handoff requirements we'd need to include for the on-prem NOC.
3) Naomi — security constraints: are egress-only TLS tunnels acceptable from a compliance standpoint for regulated customers?

I've uploaded the files here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3-edge-nat-design (PDF + PNG). Attaching lightweight stubs below.

Attachments: [controlplane_dataplane_interface_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 320KB)], [egress-nat-diagram.png (image/png, 180KB)]

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Sent: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 10:25:43 -0700
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Edge NAT + control/data-plane concordance — design review

Diego / team —

Quick notes after my pass on v2:

1) CP callback patterns:
   - Option A (persistent TLS tunnel): easiest for low-latency control messages, keeps a single upstream address for CP metrics. Requires the customer to allow outbound long-lived TLS on port 443. Heartbeats and tracing are over the same tunnel.
   - Option B (periodic outbound calls): stateless, easier for restrictive networks, but introduces 30–90s control latency for some ops tasks and complicates rolling key refresh.

2) KVCACHE concerns:
   - If we multiplex CP control over the DP NAT tunnel (Option A), we must ensure the KV cache affinity keys include the tunnel-id so we don't misroute hot prefixes across different fabric attachments.
   - Recommend adding a short (1–2 line) annotation schema to the CP metadata used in the attachment handshake (see p.3 of PDF).

3) Observability & cutover proof:
   - We need a webhook endpoint on the CP side that the on-prem agent can hit to prove successful egress. A signed timestamp + cert-fingerprint exchange should be sufficient.

I've inserted inline comments in the PDF.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in Packly Ops for their constraints — added alex.taylor@packly.io to CC.

Packly has two constraints we should bake into the doc:
- Their on-prem appliance sits in a DMZ and only allows outbound connections to a small set of FQDNs (wildcard CN not allowed).
- They want a rolling key mechanism that does not require opening inbound holes during key rotation windows.

Operational asks (for handoff doc):
- Cutover checklist (connectivity test, sampling probe, runbook link)
- A small test harness we can run (curlable endpoint + expected JSON)
- Required firewall rules and FQDN list (we should provide both IP ranges and hostnames)

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

On Tue, 13 Jun 2028 at 09:11:02 -0400, EdgeOps Packly <edgeops@packly.io> wrote:
> Hi Diego / team,
> 
> Thanks for the diagram. A few clarifying questions from our side:
> 
> 1) For Option A (persistent TLS tunnel): how does your control-plane handle reconnection storms if the DP cluster briefly loses upstream connectivity? Will you stagger reconnects?
> 2) What data do you expect to flow over the tunnel vs what stays strictly on the DP (we need to ensure no customer PII crosses the tunnel).
> 3) For the signed timestamp proof you suggested — can you provide an example payload and signing algorithm?
> 
> Attached our NAT behavior doc (we're not including it here but can share on request).
> 
> -Alex Taylor, Packly EdgeOps

-----Original Message-----
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Sent: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 17:41:00 -0700
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, EdgeOps Packly <edgeops@packly.io>
Subject: Re: Edge NAT + control/data-plane concordance — design review

Alex / team —

Great questions. Consolidating answers and next steps below so ops and security have a single reference. I've uploaded a small example payload and a sample reconnect backoff sketch to the Drive link.

Answers:
- Reconnection storms: we will implement an exponential backoff with jitter (base 1s, cap 2m) and a per-site token-bucket to rate-limit reconnect attempts from the on-prem agent. If Packly prefers, we can also stagger agent restarts during their maintenance windows.
- Data over the tunnel vs local: control-plane messages include routing control, model pinning, and telemetry metadata (no raw customer payloads). PII and inference payloads remain on-prem and never sent over the management tunnel by default — that is enforced by the agent and validated in the attestation step.
- Signed timestamp proof: example payload in Drive (JSON) — we recommend RS256; the agent will sign a short object {site_id, timestamp, nonce, cert_thumbprint} and CP will verify against the rotated public keys.

Next steps / action items:
1) Irene: finalize the annotation schema (2 fields) and drop into the PDF (target EOD Mon 17 Jun).
2) Marissa: draft the cutover checklist (we'll include the curl endpoint and expected JSON) — target Wed 19 Jun.
3) Naomi: confirm RS256 acceptable and any key rotation requirements from compliance side — target Fri 21 Jun.
4) Packly (Alex): please send the NAT behavior doc or a short list of firewall rules you can open so we can enumerate FQDN/IPs.

I'll host a 30-min sync on Tue 18 Jun at 10:00 PT to walk the diagram and run through the cutover checklist once drafts are in. Invite sent separately.

Thanks all —
Diego
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
